summary: Two blind judges (opus, sonnet) give the article of 40 segments whose tag the context-rule variant changes; a third (opus) on splits

opus.reason: Under the heading on draft ICCPR article 2: the chair weighs 'discrimination' against 'distinction' and the Japanese 'persons' amendment to article 2. Article 24 is only mentioned in passing.
The chair opens ICESCR draft article 20 and its two amendments; the numbering maps draft 20 to final ICESCR 19.
This is the debate on deleting draft ICCPR article 34 (members staying on for pending matters). The numbering lists it as former-34, with no final article.
Tunisia supports deleting draft article 34, which was dropped (former-34, no final counterpart). Article 39 comes up only in passing.
India answers the Philippines on continuity during the debate on deleting draft article 34, which has no final article.
Italy argues for keeping the deleted draft article 34 and changing 'case' to 'matter'. Article 40 is a passing mention.
Cuba's offer is about where articles 16 and 17 sit in the Declaration. It concerns the order of the articles, not their content.
The decision transmits draft Covenant article 11 (Geneva text); by subject that is freedom of movement, and its limitations are linked to article 9. The record does not name the subject.
China reserves the question of which rights cannot be derogated in war or public emergency, during the debate on the Article 4 war-and-emergency clause.
Lebanon says some rights must never be derogated even in emergencies, and the record notes how the two Article 4 (derogation) drafts were to be transmitted.

sonnet.reason: Chair on 'individuals' vs 'persons' and 'discrimination' vs 'distinction' in article 2 of the draft Covenant (draft 2 = final 2); article 24 only mentioned in passing.
Chair takes up draft ICESCR article 20 with its amendments; numbering maps draft 20 to final ICESCR 19.
Debate on deleting draft article 34 (members continuing in office); draft 34 is absent from the numbering, so no final article matches.
Tunisia favours deleting draft article 34 on practical grounds; draft 34 has no final counterpart in the numbering, so not final ICCPR 34.
India answers on continuity if draft article 34 is deleted; draft 34 is unmapped, with no final article.
Italy wants draft article 34 retained, with 'matter' for 'case'; draft 34 is unmapped, so not final ICCPR 34 (vacancies).
Cuba's offer to withdraw proposals if articles 16 and 17 keep their new position concerns the arrangement and order of articles, not content.
Procedural decision to transmit draft Article 11 with a note; the file gives no numbering or subject for it, so no final article can be named.
China reserves the question of which rights may not be derogated in war or public emergency, within discussion of the war and emergency clause (Article 4).
Lebanon says some rights must never be derogated even in war or emergency; the discussion concerns the two drafts of the emergency clause, Article 4.

third.reason: Vote transmitting draft covenant Article 11 (two paragraphs, limitations tied to Article 9 detention); fits liberty of movement, but record never names subject.

opus.reason: Under heading Article 20 (draft 20 -> UDHR 18); Chair reads it, religious groups' views, US view on wording of paragraph 2.
Harry speaks of the whole bracket of Chapter V freedoms (convention vs declaration), not specifically draft Article 20; several articles, none dominating.
Chair proposes adopting draft Article 11 (slavery -> UDHR 4), noting it covers traffic in women, servitude, forced labour.
Vote adopting text of draft Article 30 (pay, just conditions, trade unions, equal pay) -> UDHR 23; stray 'Article 34' heading misplaced.
Decision adopting the Philippines-France text of Article 1 ('born free and equal...'); trailing 'Comment on Article 36' is a following heading.
Under heading draft Article 15 (-> ICCPR 16); Philippine wording mirrors UDHR article 6, which is cited, not the subject.
Roll-call vote on USSR procedural proposal about order of work (additional articles vs Parts I and III).
Chair's closing thanks to members, officers and Secretariat at session end.
US proposal to add 'territory and subject to its jurisdiction' in draft article 2, paragraph 1 (-> ICCPR 2).
In debate on draft article 8 (forced labour); Egypt's martial-law question about article 8's scope; article 4 cited as covering it.

sonnet.reason: Chair reads draft Article 20 (freedom of worship, teaching religious belief, conscience); numbering maps draft 20 to UDHR 18.
Harry speaks of the whole bracket of Chapter V freedoms and Convention versus Declaration treatment, not one article.
Chair proposes adopting draft Article 11 on slavery, covering traffic in women and forced labour; draft 11 maps to UDHR 4.
Adopted text for draft Article 30: pay, just conditions, trade unions, women's equal pay; maps to UDHR 23. The Article 34 heading precedes it.
Vote adopting the Article 1 text (born free and equal in dignity and rights); the trailing 'Comment on Article 36' is only a following heading.
Under draft Covenant Article 15 (recognition as person before the law, from UDHR art. 6 wording); draft 15 maps to ICCPR 16.
Roll-call vote on the order of work: whether to take the additional economic and social articles before Parts I and III.
Chair's closing thanks to members, vice-presidents, rapporteur and Secretariat; purely procedural.
US amendment to draft article 2(1), 'territory and subject to its jurisdiction'; draft 2 maps to ICCPR 2.
Ramadan says martial law falls under article 4(1) (derogation), not article 8(4)(c); the debate is on article 8, but this remark turns on article 4.

third.reason: Exchange on whether martial law affects draft article 8 (forced labour); Egypt cites article 4(1) only as where his concern falls, versus 8(4)(c).

opus.reason: Ordonneau on the adequacy of draft article 17 (freedom of information) and the French text; draft 17 maps to final ICCPR 19.
Asks that the vote be taken on the French text of draft article 17 as it stands; this is about the vote on ICCPR 19.
Sorensen on draft article 20 paragraph 2: discrimination grounds, minority association, amendments; draft 20 maps to final ICCPR 26.
Defends the US 'territory and jurisdiction' amendment to article 2; the article 11 reference is in passing.
Nisot proposes wording on jurisdiction and territory for the first sentence of article 2, paragraph 1 (scope of obligations).
Chair names the open points on article 4: whether articles 9 and 20 go in the non-derogable list of paragraph 2.
Vote on the UK additional article on reservations; no final Covenant article corresponds.
Cassin on the order of work: discussing articles 20-32 entails the general clause (article 19(4)). Procedural, no single article dominates.
About whether to meet on 1 May; purely procedural.
Chair announces the end of article 27 and moves to article 31; order of work only.

sonnet.reason: French delegate on draft article 17 (freedom of information/expression), its adequacy and his text; draft 17 maps to final ICCPR 19.
Chair insists the vote be taken on the French text for draft article 17 (freedom of information); draft 17 maps to final ICCPR 19.
Danish speaker on draft article 20 paragraph 2, grounds of non-discrimination (minorities); draft 20 maps to final ICCPR 26.
Chair defends the US 'territory and jurisdiction' amendment to article 2; the reference to article 11 is incidental.
Belgian wording on persons within territory or subject to jurisdiction, in the article 2 debate; Chair's aliens reply stays on scope.
Chair recalls the open points in article 4 paragraph 2, which articles are non-derogable; heading is Articles 4 and 23; draft 4 maps to ICCPR 4.
Vote on inserting 'only' in the UK additional reservations article, a clause that did not become any final article; procedural.
Cassin on order of work: discussing articles 20-32 will involve article 19 paragraph 4, the general clause; procedural, spans many articles.
Roosevelt says the Commission should work on 1 May rather than celebrate it; purely a scheduling matter.
Chair announces end of draft article 27 and the move to article 31; an order-of-work statement naming two articles, neither dominating.

opus.reason: Continuation of the French chairman's analysis of approaches to draft article 3 (right to life) and amendments to its paragraph 2; draft 3 maps to ICCPR 6.
Poland objects to self-defence and the riot exception in draft article 3 on the right to life (draft 3 maps to ICCPR 6).
Chair invites the Rapporteur to introduce the new text of draft article 40, which the numbering maps to ICCPR 34 (filling vacancies).
UK accepts an amendment to draft article 42 on declaring a member's seat vacant; draft 42 maps to ICCPR 33.
Chile withdraws its amendment to draft article 42, paragraph 1 (removal and vacancy of a member), which maps to ICCPR 33.
Chair opens examination of draft article 69 (Charter and specialized agencies' constitutions), mapped to ICESCR 24; no amendments submitted.
USSR criticises merged draft 25/26 for dropping housing and medical care; the merged text is the ancestor of UDHR 25.
Chair explains 'social security' in merged draft 25/26 as the right to an adequate standard of living; the text became UDHR 25.
Chair calls on an NGO to speak on draft article 6 (mutilation, experimentation), which the numbering maps to ICCPR 7.
China supports reproducing UDHR article 5 in draft article 7 and deleting draft 6 for now; both map to ICCPR 7.

sonnet.reason: Chair Cassin continues his analysis of the three approaches to draft article 3 (right to life), which maps to final ICCPR 6.
Boratynski objects to self-defence and riot exceptions in draft article 3 on the right to life, which maps to ICCPR 6.
Chair invites the Rapporteur to present the new text for draft article 40, which the numbering maps to ICCPR 34; the line gives no content.
Hoare accepts a Chilean amendment to draft article 42 on vacancies (unanimity vs two-thirds); draft 42 maps to ICCPR 33.
Chile withdraws its unanimity proposal to the UK text of draft article 42 on vacating a Committee seat; draft 42 maps to ICCPR 33.
Chair opens examination of draft article 69 (UN Charter and specialized agencies' constitutions), which maps to ICESCR 24.
Pavlov complains housing and medical assistance were dropped and questions 'security'; this is mostly standard-of-living wording (UDHR 25), though joint 25/26 text also touches social security.
Chair equates 'right to social security' with standard of living and social services in the merged draft 25/26; this straddles UDHR 22 and 25 with neither dominating.
Chair invites a statement on draft article 6 (sterilization, mutilation, experiments), which maps to ICCPR 7.
Chang backs reproducing UDHR art. 5 in draft article 7 and deleting article 6 for now; both draft 6 and 7 map to ICCPR 7.

third.reason: Chair interprets wording of combined draft Articles 25/26 (standard of living, social services, security against unemployment), which became UDHR 25.
